titleEn: I Can Do It—I'm a Big Brother!

pages.text: "Mom, look at me!" Dari bounced in the bedroom, but Mom only patted Kongal. "Quiet. Kongal's sleeping." Dari pouted. His heart hurt.
"I hate Kongal! Everyone loves only Kongal!" Dari pounded the floor with his flippers. "Hug me, too! I'm here!" He hid under the quilt.
Underneath was dark and quiet. Outside came Kongal's giggles and Mom's laughter. Spring sunlight filled the round window. Only Dari was alone, head and tail drooping.
Mom lifted the quilt. "You're a big brother now. There are things only a big brother can do." She held his flipper. "You can do it! Shall we try?"
Mom took him to the cradle. Kongal was crying. "Why?" Dari looked carefully. "The quilt's come off?" Little back flippers waved outside it.
Dari gently pulled the quilt over Kongal's back flippers. Crying stopped—and giggles began! A little flipper gripped his. Dari's angry feeling melted away.
"Mom! I helped Kongal stop crying!" Proud shoulders, excited heart! Dari slapped his tail. "I can do it—I'm a big brother! I'm best at this!"
Being a big brother was fun now. Peekaboo made Kongal smile; songs made the baby's back flippers tap. Kongal's eyes followed only Dari.

When Mom cuddled Kongal, Dari no longer sulked. "Three big-brother jobs! One, see why the baby's crying. Two, pull up the quilt. Three, sing a lullaby!" He sang beside the cradle. Kongal's eyes slowly closed.
Mom hugged Dari and Kongal together. "A proper big brother now!" A new sibling brought special things Dari could do, instead of only jealousy. "I can do it—I'm a big brother!"
